full_judgment:
23. He refers to actions of the Government as to removal of the public prosecutors namely, Mosharraf Hossain Kajal and Shahara Khatun, Advocates and also removal of special public prosecutors namely Anisul Haque and Syed Rezaur Rahman, Advocates by special order and submits that above actions of the Government also indicated ill motive of the authority and the same might reasonably have created apprehension that fair and impartial trial and disposal of the above case would be impossible by any of the courts subordinate to the High Court as because due to non-implementation of the Historical Judgment of the Honorable Appellate Division in Masder Hossain case by the present Government as to separation of the Judiciary from Executive there would be probability of skillful interference in the trial of the present Jail Killing case by any Sessions Division inasmuch as all Judicial Officers have been directly under the control of the Executive (Ministry of Law and Justice) for their appointed posting, promotion and transfer, etc. He accordingly, submits that above facts justify the apprehension of the petitioner as to non-getting of fair and impartial trial of the case by any Sessions Divisions of the country including Dhaka other than High Court Division itself. He submits that when section 526(i)(e)(iii) contains clear provision for trial and disposal of any Sessions or criminal case by High Court Division on being transferred to itself as a court of first instance, the appeal against any order of conviction and sentence awarded in the above trial by High Court Division itself would lie as of right in the Appellate Division under provisions of Article 103(2)(b) of the Constitution. 

 24. In order to strengthen his above contention on the point, learned Advocate refers to the decision in the case of Moyna Miah and others vs State reported in 27 DLR (AD) 120 and shows from paragraph II (b) of the said decision that the expression "sentenced a person to death or to transportation for life," occurring in sub-clause 2(b) of Article 103 of the Constitution will cover cases where as a court of first instance the High Court Division sentences a person to death or to transportation for life. Accordingly, he submits that in the event of conviction and sentence to either death or imprisonment for life of any person after holding trial of a case as a court of first instance by the High Court Division on transfer to itself under section 526(1)(e)(iii) of the Code, the convict as of right can have the scope to prefer appeal to the Appellate Division under Article 103(2)(b) of the Constitution. 

 39. On behalf of State opposite party it has been further submitted that Article 103(1)(b) of the Constitution provides that an appeal will lie to Appellate Division as of right when High Court Division sentenced a person to death or imprisonment for life on transfer of a case to itself under provision of section 526(1)(e)(iii) of the Code of Criminal Procedure. But it has been argued that nothing was disclosed clearly under what circumstances such trial can be held by High Court Division on transfer of a particular case to itself. It has been also argued that in the cited decision on behalf of petitioner reported in 27 DLR (AD) 120 there has been no clear indication about circumstances under which trial of a particular case can be held by High Court Division as a Court of first instance to sentence a person to death or to imprisonment for life when the appeal against that order of conviction and sentence may be to the separate Division under Article 103(2)(b) of the Constitution. 

 57. It is true that in the event of any such trial by High Court Division on transfer of any particular case to itself under section 526(1)(e)(iii) of the Code it will be deemed that such trial will be held by the High Court Division as a court of first instance. In such context if after such trial, High Court Division sentences any person to death or imprisonment for life, then against such order of conviction and sentence appeal will be to the Appellate Division under Article 103(2)(b) of the Constitution which runs as follows; 

 "103(2) An appeal to the Appellate Division from judgment, decree, order or sentence of High Court Division shall lie as of right where High Court Division  …………….. 

 58. Applicability of provisions of Article 103(2)(b) of the Constitution was thoroughly discussed in the decision of the case of Moyna Meah and others vs State reported in 27 DLR (AD) 120 as cited on behalf of petitioner at the hearing. In paragraph 11(b) of the above decision Honorable Appellate Division observed as below: 

 The expression "sentenced a person to death or to transportation for life." occurring in the aforesaid sub-clause of Article 103 covers cases where High Court Division in exercise of its powers under section passed by the trial Court to a sentence of death or transportation for life or where the High Court Division after setting aside an order of acquittal passed by the trial Court, convicts the accused and sentences him to death or to transportation for life or where as a court of first instance the High Court Division sentences a person to death or to transportation for life."
